title: ZIA Advanced Threat Protection
aliases: why is this blocked as a threat

prose.text: "Why was this blocked as a threat?" and "what is ATP set to?" are answered in a fixed order. ATP is the policy of inline URL, content and behavior detections; file scanning is [[zia.malware-protection]], and which engine produced a block is read from the log: [[zia.atp.block-diagnosis]], [[zia.sandbox.verdicts]].
{{global-policy}} {{no-scoping}} {{before-ips}} IPS Control itself is covered in [[zia.firewall.ips]].

steps.label: Which detection fired?
steps.text: The toggles and their groups: [[zia.atp.categories]], with the Page Risk threshold in [[zia.atp.page-risk]], C2 and DGA in [[zia.atp.botnet]], country blocking in [[zia.atp.blocked-countries]] and Tor in [[zia.atp.tor]].

steps.label: Is a list involved?
steps.text: The tenant denylist is [[zia.atp.blocked-urls]]; the allowlist is [[zia.atp.security-exceptions]].

steps.label: Did the policy change at all?
steps.text: A URL can start blocking with no edit: [[zia.atp.ai-ml-recategorization]].

steps.label: Where does it run?
steps.text: The order of checks, and what an exception skips: [[zia.atp.enforcement-order]]. Content detections need decryption: [[zia.ssl-inspection.bypass-impact]].

prose.text: API and field-name traps are in [[zia.atp.api-surface]]; provider defects are in [[zia.terraform.multi-step-writes]], [[zia.terraform.error-handling]] and [[zia.terraform.activation]].

global-policy.statement: Advanced Threat Protection is a global policy that applies to all users.

quotes: The Advanced Threat Protection policy is a global policy, so it applies to all users.

no-scoping.statement: There is no per-user, per-group or per-location scope for ATP: each toggle is on or off for the whole tenant, and the API is one settings object plus two URL lists.
no-scoping.conditions: Derived from the policy being global; no source describes a scoping control and none was found in the help page or the API.

before-ips.statement: When a tenant has both Advanced Threat Protection and IPS Control, the rules created for Advanced Threat Protection are evaluated first.

quotes: If you have Advanced Threat Protection as well as IPS Control, any rules you create for Advanced Threat Protection are evaluated first.

recommended-policy.statement: The recommended policy sets Page Risk to 35; in Botnet Protection it blocks Command & Control Servers, Command & Control Traffic and Domain Generation Algorithm (DGA) Domains and enables Alert for Unknown/Suspicious C2 Traffic; it blocks everything in Malicious Active Content, Fraud, Unauthorized Communication and XSS protection, and blocks BitTorrent, Tor and Google Hangouts.

quotes: Alert for Unknown/Suspicious C2 Traffic: Enabled
Malicious Active Content Protection: Block all

client-connector-notice.statement: When ATP blocks malicious activity matching a user's traffic, Zscaler Client Connector shows a notification that the activity was blocked as potentially harmful.

quotes: Zscaler Client Connector displays a notification that the activity was blocked as potentially harmful.

save-and-activate.statement: A change to the policy is saved and then activated in the console.

quotes: Click Save and activate the change.
